html:
The Cape Fear Indians were a small Native people who lived near the mouth of the Cape Fear River in what is now southeastern North Carolina. Their own name is not known; English settlers named them after the cape.

They were probably Siouan speakers like their neighbours the Waccamaw and Pee Dee. An English colony from Barbados settled briefly on the river in 1664 and quarrelled with them over captives; it was abandoned in 1667. Wars and slave raids of the early 1700s, including the Yamasee War of 1715, broke them up, and they disappear from the records later in that century.
